instruction: Change the file extensions of all images in my Pictures directory from lowercase .jpg to uppercase .JPG.

result.command: cd /home/user/Pictures && (for f in *.JPG *.jpg 2>/dev/null; do [ -f "$f" ] && sha256sum "$f"; done) | python3 -c "import sys,json; lines = [l.strip().split(None, 1) for l in sys.stdin if l.strip()]; print(json.dumps({line[0]: line[1] for line in lines if len(line) == 2}))"

metadata.explanation: Task requires changing file extensions from .jpg to .JPG for all 3 images. Evaluator uses inline shell command to compute SHA256 hashes of all JPG/jpg files in /home/user/Pictures/ and outputs JSON mapping {hash: filename}. Metric function verifies that all 3 expected image hashes map to filenames ending with '.JPG'.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly uses content-based verification: SHA256 hashes identify files by content, not name - this is the semantically correct approach for verifying file renames

Metric logic is correct: Properly handles 'expected' parameter (direct access to rules dict, no Section 5.1 violations), verifies all expected image hashes exist in result, and checks each hash maps to filename ending with '.JPG'
